{{nihongo|'''Tanabata Shrine'''|多奈波太神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Owari Province]].

'''Tanabata Shrine''' (たなばたじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in Kinjo 4-chōme, {{ill|Kita-ku, Nagoya|Q1207964|qid=Q1207964|lt=Kita Ward}}, {{ill|Nagoya|Q11751|qid=Q11751}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|Q80434|qid=Q80434}}. It is identified with "Tanabata Shrine" of Yamada District, {{ill|Owari Province|Q514506|qid=Q514506}}, in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}.

=== History ===
Until the {{ill|Edo period|lt=Edo period|qid=Q184963}}, it was called '''Tendō'''. It is said that in the Sengoku period, during a punitive burning by {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|Q171411|qid=Q171411}}, the shrine buildings and transmitted documents were burned, so the founding year is unknown. The early-Edo ''{{ill|Kanbunmuramuraoboegaki|Q137766629|qid=Q137766629}}'' records "Tabata village... Tendō... Bizen exemption." It is also said that when {{ill|Nagoya Castle|Q648629|qid=Q648629}} was built, the shrine was moved to its current site by land substitution. {{ill|Tsuda Masanari|Q22123474|qid=Q22123474}} mentioned a theory that in earlier times it was located in "Ofuke no kaku-nai" (possibly in present {{ill|Meijō Park|Q6810044|qid=Q6810044}}). Around the current shrine is the Tanabatachō archaeological site where {{ill|Yayoi pottery|Q11487461|qid=Q11487461}} has been excavated.

In the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, it came under the control of {{ill|Nagoya Tōshō-gū|Q3335117|qid=Q3335117}}, and during the {{ill|Kan'ei|Q1192913|qid=Q1192913}} era new shrine buildings were constructed by the {{ill|Owari Domain|Q1062072|qid=Q1062072}}. On the annual festival day of the old lunar {{ill|July 7 (Lunisolar)|Q839741|qid=Q839741|lt=7th day of the 7th month}}, the domain lord visited and ordinary townspeople were also permitted to worship inside the enclosure; many records survive, including depictions in the {{ill|Owari meisho zue|Q11465290|qid=Q11465290}}.

After it was identified in the Edo period with Yamada District's "Tanabata Shrine" in the Engishiki Jinmyōchō, this became the accepted theory. In the {{ill|Owari Kokunai Jinmyōchō|Q11041830|qid=Q11041830}} it appears as "Junior Third Rank Upper, Keta-hata Tenjin," suggesting the shikinaisha Tanabata Shrine was also called Keta-hata Tenjin. The main reason this shrine was identified as Tanabata Shrine is that it was located in Tabata Village of {{ill|Kasugai district|Q11513576|qid=Q11513576}}, with similar village and shrine names. The {{ill|Chōshūfushi|Q137847623|qid=Q137847623}} identifies Tanabata Shrine with Sansha Myōjin in {{ill|Obata|Q52158082|qid=Q52158082|lt=Obata Village}}, but late-Edo gazetteers including {{ill|Owarishi|Q137855962|qid=Q137855962}} consistently identify this shrine as Tanabata Shrine.

In the {{ill|Meiji era|lt=Meiji period|qid=Q3125096}}, when the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} was implemented, it became a village shrine under the name Hachiman Shrine; in {{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}} 11 ({{ill|1922|Q2165|qid=Q2165}}) it became a designated village shrine. During {{ill|World War II|Q362|qid=Q362}}, an {{ill|anti-aircraft gun|Q21156889|qid=Q21156889}} battery was placed on shrine grounds, and much of the shrine forest known as "Tanabata Forest" was cut down. In the {{ill|Bombing of Nagoya|Q2813858|qid=Q2813858}} of May 14, {{ill|1945|Q5240|qid=Q5240}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 20), the same raid that destroyed Nagoya Castle's main keep, the shrine buildings were burned down. The current buildings were rebuilt in {{ill|1964|Q2652|qid=Q2652}} (Shōwa 39).

=== Festivals ===
* Monthly festival: every month on the 7th
* Jan 1 - New Year Festival
* Jan 14 - Sagichō Festival
* Mar 7 - Kinen Festival
* Jul 7 - Chinowa Festival
* Aug 7 - Annual Grand Festival
* Oct 7 - Prayer Festival
* Dec 7 - Niiname Festival
* Dec 30 - Great Purification Festival

=== Access ===
* {{ill|Nagoya Municipal Subway|Q1144874|qid=Q1144874}}{{ill|Meijō Line|Q906775|qid=Q906775|lt=Meijō Line}} - about 10 minutes on foot from Exit 2 of {{ill|Meijō Kōen Station|Q863874|qid=Q863874}}.
* {{ill|Nagoya Municipal Bus|Q11414982|qid=Q11414982}} - get off at "Jōhokubashi" on Sakae 11 / Sakae 25 routes, about 5 minutes on foot.
